$comment: Design-System Alignment scores (roadmap 92.3). SOURCE OF TRUTH for what renders on component pages — never hand-type a score into a page. Each dimension is 0-3 with a checkable citation; `na` leaves the denominator. Full reasoning lives in .roundtable/scorecard-*.md; this file carries what the docs display. Re-take a score when a component's design changes. `scored` is the date of the entry's last FULL pass over all six dimensions — move it when you re-take the whole entry. A SINGLE dimension re-scored later keeps its date in its own cite and does NOT move `scored`, because moving it would claim the other five were re-taken that day — the independent second opinion LOOPS.md §3b step 4 requires, and which nobody gave. The sentence this replaces said the opposite (`update scored to that date`), and it was correctly disobeyed on 2 of 2 occasions where it applied: `breadcrumb · interaction` (na->3, blind re-scored 2026-09-04, entry stamped 2026-08-21) and `dashboard · interaction` (na->3, 2026-09-02, stamped 2026-08-23). So a page can publish `Alignment scored <full-pass date>` beside a cite naming a later re-score, and that is correct rather than a contradiction. Recorded 2026-09-04 (roadmap 269.1).

definitions.$comment: What earns 3 on each dimension, and what a FAILURE looks like (roadmap 94.7). Written because three dimensions had scored 3 on 28 of 28 components — a value that never varies is not a measurement. Each definition names a component in this repo that scores below 3, so the dimension is known to be capable of failing.
definitions.typography: 3 = sizes come from the type scale or a density alias; an em RATIO counts too when the element must track its host rather than the document — inline mono correcting an optical mismatch, an affix subordinate to its value, text fitting inside a box. Those cannot use an absolute step, and each must say so in place, exactly as spacing requires of intrinsic dimensions. Below 3 = a raw size that IS a scale step in disguise, or an unexplained one. Resolved in 94.13: the six raw sizes split into one genuine token (--bo-font-size-mono-inline, 3 callers that had disagreed 0.85 vs 0.9) and three explained intrinsics.
definitions.colour: 3 = zero raw colour outside @media print / forced-colors, and any state signal is two-channel. Below 3 = a raw colour on screen, or meaning carried by hue alone.
definitions.spacing: 3 = dimensions come from space tokens, or an intrinsic literal carries a comment saying why it is intrinsic. NOTE: this is a DEBT MARKER, not a quality signal — it is satisfiable by the scorer writing the comment, and once written it stays 3 forever. Read it as "has this file been through a scoring pass", not as "is this well spaced".
definitions.interaction: 3 = the page states what the PLATFORM provides versus what the behavior adds, so a reader knows what they lose by not running the JS; a component that ships NO behavior earns 3 by saying so. `na` only when there is no interaction surface at all. Below 3 = a behavior-backed component whose page never draws that line. Applied by READING all 14 behaviour-backed pages in 94.9, not by grep — an earlier regex was wrong on 4 of 7. The three that failed (alert, combobox, tree-table) were fixed in 94.14; the dimension has demonstrated it can fail.
definitions.content: 3 = the opener carries the wrong-choice clause the recipe requires — a <strong> clause beginning "Not "/"Never "/"Do not" naming a context where this component is the WRONG choice, plus the alternative. Below 3 = it does not. GOALPOST MOVED, deliberately and on the record: 94.7 defined this as "names a wrong-choice context" in prose, and 94.10 made the clause the mandated form because 34 of 40 pages had nothing and a prose-only rule could not be enforced. check:wrong-choice is the executable version of this definition, so the score and the gate agree by construction; check-dsa-scores asserts they cannot drift apart. EXEMPT pages (button, form, prose) score 3 — no wrong context exists for them.
definitions.fit: 3 = the docs prescribe the contexts the component belongs to, including where it does NOT belong. The field matrix on /concepts/design-language is the authority WHERE IT REACHES — its four field types (Date, Number/rate/%, Money, Quantity) across its four contexts (standalone form entry / read-mostly record-table / editable table / display). Measured, it reaches 4 of the 40 components carrying this score: amount, form, money and quantity are the only scored components the matrix section links (`/components/([a-z0-9-]+)` over the section between 'The field matrix' and 'Subtraction is the method'; it also links inline-editing, which carries no score). For the other 36 the context set is the component's own neighbourhood — the screens or regions the docs place it in, plus the neighbouring component the page names as the different job (combobox vs dropdown, skeleton vs state, progress vs stepper, prose vs richtext, tag-input vs combobox). 0 = prescribed in no context at all. Fails today: date (deprecated, zero screens use it) — and note the matrix carries a Date ROW while linking no date component page, the same reach gap seen from the other side. CORRECTED 2026-09-06 (roadmap 286.4): this read "the contexts the field matrix assigns it", a four-row reference set that cannot assign a context to 36 of the 40 components it is applied to — filed by 279.2 against `scan` and passed on because 101.3 forbids a Polish round editing a rubric definition. The cost was not hypothetical: `scan`'s own fit cite claimed it was "prescribed where the field matrix puts it" while `scan` appears **0** times anywhere on that page, corrected in this same commit. The matrix was NOT widened to fit the rubric — it covers field types, and scan is an input mechanism.
definitions.$retired: hierarchy — RETIRED 2026-08-21 (roadmap 94.9). It scored 3 on every one of the 25 components it applied to and never once varied, even after 94.7 narrowed it to `na` where a component presents fewer than two affordances. Retiring it loses nothing, which is the point: the property it named — at most one visually primary action — is measured where it actually means something, across whole SCREENS, by the design-grill baseline (roadmap 57.3, re-verified 63.2: 19 of 19 pattern screens, with wizard Next/Submit and master-detail Save-in-dialog recorded as the two legitimate exceptions). A component almost never presents two competing primaries because a component is not a screen. Do not re-add it without a component that fails it.

scope.$comment: Which ARTIFACT each dimension is scored on (roadmap 292.3, 2026-09-06). `css` = the component's shipped stylesheet under packages/core/src/css/components/<name>/. `page` = its docs page under apps/docs/src/pages/components/. Raised by a blind re-score that scored one surface 2 or 3 depending on the answer and could not resolve it from the text above. MEASURED BEFORE BEING WRITTEN, over all 240 cites (40 components x 6 dimensions), classified by which artifact the cite names: typography/colour/spacing are 120 of 120 css-side and 0 docs-page-side, so the scope was already unambiguous in PRACTICE and only the text was silent. The asymmetry is exact — interaction/content/fit each already name their subject in `definitions` above ('the page', 'opener', 'the docs'); colour named no subject at all, and typography and spacing named one only obliquely ('in place', 'this file'). Three cites a keyword pass flagged as naming both artifacts (typography/scan, colour/offcanvas, colour/dialog) say 'the page' meaning the CONSUMER's page, and two it flagged as naming neither (spacing/richtext, spacing/dropdown) are css-side in phrasing too terse to match; hand-read against the text, the trio is 40/40/40. The scope is stated HERE and deliberately not repeated into the six `definitions` — two records of one fact is how they drift, which is the defect 4c in check-dsa-scores.mjs exists to prevent between the score and the gate. Consequence, stated because it is why the question was asked: a raw font-size in a docs PAGE is outside `typography` entirely — icon.astro is the only one of 41 component pages carrying any, and no gate polices docs-page style (filed as roadmap 292.8).

rubric.stopRule: roadmap 101.3 (2026-08-22). This rubric produced its own follow-up chain nine times in a row (94.7 -> 94.9/94.10 -> 94.11/94.12 -> 94.14) and is now complete enough to STOP investing in by default. FIRES another rubric change only when a live grill (not a re-score) finds a component/pattern that scores 3 across the board yet has a genuine, user-facing defect the six dimensions structurally cannot see as currently defined — the worked example is 102.7's forms-family grill, which found `form.astro`'s `--required` demo shipping the visible asterisk with zero `aria-required`, a defect none of typography/colour/spacing/interaction/content/fit is written to catch. The mirror case — a component scoring low that a grill shows is actually fine — fires it too. DOES NOT fire on: a dimension reading uniformly across components (documented in 94.7/94.9 as an expected, honest property once a definition is sharp, not evidence of a broken rubric — see `hierarchy`'s retirement and `content`'s 94.8 clearance); or a grill that CONFIRMS the rubric's existing verdict rather than contradicting it (102.2's object-page grill and 102.3's editable-grid grill both did this — all-3s held, nothing added). Until the trigger fires, scoring work is maintenance of the existing ratchet only (fixing entries the rubric already flags) — new dimensions, definitions, or gates are out of scope, and the queue belongs to whatever the owner actually asked for.

spacing.cite: 94.3 moved the two auto-compaction heights OUT of this file — row and control height are set from --bo-density-auto-* in tokens/density.css, beside the tiers they relate to — so data-table.css carries no height literal at all (re-verified 2026-09-05: 0 height-family declarations carrying a unit literal, against 15 of 44 component stylesheets that carry one). What it carries is the reason (94.2), corrected by roadmap 281.1 after re-measuring it live: raising cell-padding-x to compact's --bo-space-2 at 390px grows a row whose cells WRAP by ~19-20px (68px to 87px on /components/dialog and /components/state-patterns, `a24ed45`), while a row that does not wrap is held at the row-height floor and goes 28px to 30px on the auto-vs-compact row height alone — padding plays no part in that half, and 94.3's single sentence read as though it did. So the tighter padding buys horizontal room, the scarce resource at phone width. 94.3's cited example page, /patterns/detail-form, no longer SHOWS the step — but it is still REACHED by the rule, and 281.1's stated cause is refuted (roadmap 286.1): `69a53364` (109.19) is a pure addition, 91 insertions and 0 deletions, that added a different table and never touched this one, which is unchanged since 94.3 (5 th, 3 tr, 26 lines) and still carries no data-density. What moved is the baseline, not the reach: at 390px the reached table measures 260px against its three siblings' 310px and its first row already wraps at 87px before any mutation, so it cannot produce a 68px -> 87px step. The example is now named by property, not by page.
